newsitem.title: UK: UK opposition welcomes report on energy regulation.
newsitem.headline: UK opposition welcomes report on energy regulation.

text.p: The opposition UK Labour Party on Tuesday welcomed parliament's trade and industry committee report on energy regulation.

"There is a growing consensus of the need to reform utility regulation to put the consumer first," said John Battle, Labour's energy minister, in a statement. "The Select Committee's report is a welcome contribution to that debate".

Among its 35 recommendations the all-party committee said Stephen Littlechild, director general of electricity supply, should consider adopting further measures to accelerate the development of effective competition in Britain's electricity generation industry.
The committee, however, sidestepped Labour's controversial plan to levy a windfall tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities.
Separately, the Gas Consumers Council (GCC) said it believed many of the report's recommendations contribute to the future of regulation and will enhance consumer protection.

"In particular we welcome the call for greater openness on the part of the monopoly in moving to an assumption that information will be public unless it can be proven to be confidential," GCC said in a statement.
